subject: Procurement path for EU healthcare: marketplace listing vs direct contract
messages:
From: Martin Olofsson <martin.olofsson@acmehealth.eu>

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Procurement channel question — marketplace listing vs direct contract

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement here at Acme Health has a couple of gating questions before we advance to legal/PO:

1) For customers in the EU with regulated health data, is it possible to buy via Azure/AWS marketplace and still have the billing/invoice hit our finance team without introducing a third-party reseller that would change data residency or support SLAs?

2) What does the marketplace route mean for co-sell incentives and any reseller/partner approvals — will there be an additional onboarding step that delays start-of-service?

3) If we need an MSA redline or specific DPAs, is the private-offer/direct procurement route recommended versus the standard marketplace listing?

We can share a short RFI (attached) and would appreciate a short note on tradeoffs so procurement can decide which lane to route the vendor through.

Best,
Martin
Martin Olofsson
Senior Procurement Manager | Acme Health

Subject: Re: Procurement channel question — marketplace listing vs direct contract

Martin —

Thanks for the clear list — good questions. High level summary up-front: for regulated EU healthcare workloads the safest and fastest procurement lane for legal/data-residency control is a direct/private-offer (MSA + DPA) route. Marketplace can work but typically requires careful scoping to avoid unexpected reseller terms or billing flows. Details below.

Marketplace (Azure/AWS/GCP):
- Pros: faster for purchase approvals where finance requires marketplace invoices; single-click procurement for buyers already using the marketplace; can preserve buyer's invoice cadence if you opt for marketplace direct billing (seller as vendor-of-record).
- Cons: some public marketplace listings use reseller chains or marketplace-managed billing that can change seller-of-record; that can complicate EU-only data residency guarantees and custom DPAs. Private offers in marketplace (Azure private offers / AWS Marketplace private offers) can mitigate this, but they require partner setup and approval which adds 3–10 business days on average.
- Co-sell: co-sell incentives typically still apply but need partner enrollment and the private-offer must be registered. That registration step can add coordination time.

Direct / Private contract (Redwood MSA + DPA, invoiced directly):
- Pros: full control over MSA terms, DPA, KMS/HSM integration clauses, on-prem/VPC deployment language, and statement of data residency. Simpler for legal because we can accept and negotiate redlines directly.
- Cons: longer PO/finance processing for buyers who mandate marketplace purchases (they may need a legal exception).

Operational notes: if you require a strict EU-only data path we recommend including the deployment and logging residency language in the SOW and DPA. We can also provide our SOC2 report (attached) and an Azure private-offer draft so procurement can review exact invoice language.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Let us know if Acme requires marketplace ordering by policy (we can then push the Azure private-offer path and coordinate partner registration).
2) If not required, we prepare a direct MSA + DPA draft (we can accept some redlines) and provide a customer invoice sample to show finance how billing will appear.
3) I’ll loop in our partner operations contact if private-offer is preferred.

Happy to hop on a 20-min call today or tomorrow to align.

—Kimberly

Subject: Re: Procurement channel question — procurement & co-sell implications

Martin / Kimberly — quick addition from the co-sell side:

If Acme prefers marketplace for procurement convenience, the optimal path is an Azure private offer where we are the seller-of-record and Acme receives the invoice directly from us. That preserves invoice cadence for your finance team while keeping contractual control. Practical notes:
- Private offer creation requires our partner ops (can move fast) and an acceptance flow on Acme's side (buyer acceptance + any coupon/private-offer code).
- For co-sell credits and GTM motions, registration of the private-offer in the marketplace (and early notification to our partner rep) ensures co-sell tracking — otherwise, co-sell incentives could be reduced or delayed.
- If purchase must be through a specific reseller or marketplace reseller agreement, we will need to review the reseller terms to ensure they don't alter data handling clauses.

Jonas
Senior Director, Channel Sales | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Procurement channel question — legal / DPA comments

Martin —

Following up with legal/contracting guidance. Short answers:
- If Acme requires a bespoke DPA with EU-specific SIAs, direct contracting is simplest. We can incorporate EU-specific subprocessor lists and data localization clauses into the DPA.
- For private offers via marketplace, we can attach our standard DPA and a bespoke addendum; however, marketplaces occasionally limit what language may be surfaced in the purchase flow, so we prefer direct MSA + DPA for strict regulatory requirements.
- Regarding audit and evidence: we can provide the full SOC2 report and a supported-logs export procedure. If Acme needs an on-site or third-party audit clause, we can negotiate.

If you share the specific DPA redlines, we’ll produce an annotated draft within 2 business days.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Director, Legal & Compliance | Redwood Inference
